Then you copy it, build it, deploy it, debug it, and iterate manually. The feedback loop is broken.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ekube-pilot closes the loop. It lives inside the cluster with direct access to every tool in your dev stack — git, CI/CD, container registry, deployment pipelines, kubectl, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki. You communicate with it through the tools you already use (GitHub, Slack*, Jira*), and it acts with all the tools in your cluster.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCode generation tools\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ekube-pilot\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eGenerates code\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eGenerates code\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou build it\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eBuilds it (Tekton + Kaniko)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou deploy it\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDeploys it (git push + ArgoCD)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou debug it\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eQueries Prometheus + Loki, reads logs, fixes, redeploys\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou verify it\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCurls endpoints, checks metrics, verifies alerts clear\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou close the ticket\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCloses the ticket\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou wake up at 3am\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAlertmanager wakes \u003cem\u003eit\u003c/em\u003e up — it investigates and fixes autonomously\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eYou provision infra manually\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eProvisions VPCs, databases, clusters via Crossplane — from a GitHub issue\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt's not an ops bot. It's not a chatbot with kubectl access. It's an autonomous engineer that happens to live inside your cluster — and it can provision the cloud infrastructure that cluster runs on.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy Kubernetes is the perfect reasoning surface\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-kubernetes-is-the-perfect-reasoning-surface\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why Kubernetes is the perfect reasoning surface\" href=\"#why-kubernetes-is-the-perfect-reasoning-surface\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eKubernetes clusters are already built around the primitives that autonomous agents need: declarative state, observable outcomes, and deterministic tooling. Every action has a verifiable result — \u003ccode\u003ekubectl get pods\u003c/code\u003e tells you if the deploy worked, \u003ccode\u003ecurl /healthz\u003c/code\u003e tells you if the service is alive, build logs tell you exactly what failed. There's no ambiguity.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis is what makes Kubernetes fundamentally different from a local dev environment as a substrate for automation. The entire dev stack — git, CI/CD, container builds, deployment, networking, observability — is API-addressable and composable. Secrets stay behind Vault where the agent never sees them — it creates ExternalSecret references, not raw credentials. An LLM doesn't need a GUI or IDE. It needs tools that take structured input and return structured output. That's what Kubernetes is.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ekube-pilot doesn't bolt automation onto an existing workflow. It uses the cluster itself as the reasoning environment — every tool call produces observable state that feeds back into the next decision. With Crossplane, this extends beyond the cluster boundary — the agent provisions cloud infrastructure (VPCs, databases, entire Kubernetes clusters) using the same kubectl interface, the same GitOps workflow, and the same observable status conditions. The cluster isn't just where code runs. It's where the agent thinks — and from where it builds the rest of your infrastructure.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" <blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>This is a proof of concept.</strong> It works — we've deployed a full multi-service app from scratch on a single k3s node — but it's early. Expect rough edges.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>An autonomous software agent that runs in your Kubernetes cluster with access to all your dev tools.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">There's no UI. You talk to it the way you already work — file a GitHub issue, and it picks it up, writes the code, builds the container, deploys it, verifies it's running, and closes the ticket. If it crashes, it reads the logs, fixes the bug, and redeploys. When an alert fires at 3am, it wakes up, queries the metrics, reads the logs, and fixes the problem before you check your phone. Need a new database or a whole Kubernetes cluster in the cloud? It provisions real infrastructure through Crossplane — VPCs, RDS instances, GKE clusters — all via GitOps, all from a GitHub issue.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What makes this different</h2><a id="user-content-what-makes-this-different" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What makes this different" href="#what-makes-this-different"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Code generation tools generate code. Then you copy it, build it, deploy it, debug it, and iterate manually. The feedback loop is broken.</p>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot closes the loop. It lives inside the cluster with direct access to every tool in your dev stack — git, CI/CD, container registry, deployment pipelines, kubectl, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki. You communicate with it through the tools you already use (GitHub, Slack*, Jira*), and it acts with all the tools in your cluster.</p>

<p dir="auto">It's not an ops bot. It's not a chatbot with kubectl access. It's an autonomous engineer that happens to live inside your cluster — and it can provision the cloud infrastructure that cluster runs on.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Kubernetes is the perfect reasoning surface</h3><a id="user-content-why-kubernetes-is-the-perfect-reasoning-surface" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Kubernetes is the perfect reasoning surface" href="#why-kubernetes-is-the-perfect-reasoning-surface"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Kubernetes clusters are already built around the primitives that autonomous agents need: declarative state, observable outcomes, and deterministic tooling. Every action has a verifiable result — <code>kubectl get pods</code> tells you if the deploy worked, <code>curl /healthz</code> tells you if the service is alive, build logs tell you exactly what failed. There's no ambiguity.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is what makes Kubernetes fundamentally different from a local dev environment as a substrate for automation. The entire dev stack — git, CI/CD, container builds, deployment, networking, observability — is API-addressable and composable. Secrets stay behind Vault where the agent never sees them — it creates ExternalSecret references, not raw credentials. An LLM doesn't need a GUI or IDE. It needs tools that take structured input and return structured output. That's what Kubernetes is.</p>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot doesn't bolt automation onto an existing workflow. It uses the cluster itself as the reasoning environment — every tool call produces observable state that feeds back into the next decision. With Crossplane, this extends beyond the cluster boundary — the agent provisions cloud infrastructure (VPCs, databases, entire Kubernetes clusters) using the same kubectl interface, the same GitOps workflow, and the same observable status conditions. The cluster isn't just where code runs. It's where the agent thinks — and from where it builds the rest of your infrastructure.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The agent loop</h3><a id="user-content-the-agent-loop" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The agent loop" href="#the-agent-loop"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot is a tool-calling agent backed by an LLM. It receives a task, decides what tools to call (<code>exec</code>, <code>git_comment</code>, <code>read_file</code>, <code>create_pr</code>, etc.), executes them, observes the results, and iterates. If a build fails, it reads the logs and fixes the code. If a deployment crashes, it checks <code>kubectl describe</code> and adjusts the manifests. It runs up to 75 steps before giving up.</p>

<tr>
<td><strong>Vault</strong></td>

<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Traefik</strong></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>cert-manager</strong></td>
<td>Automatic TLS certificates via Let's Encrypt (optional)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>ExternalDNS</strong></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Prometheus</strong></td>

</tr>

</tr>

<p dir="auto">Everything runs in-cluster. No public URLs. No SaaS accounts. No Docker Hub. With Crossplane, kube-pilot reaches out to provision cloud infrastructure — but the control plane stays in your cluster.</p>

<p dir="auto">kube-pilot remembers what it learns. If it discovers that a repo needs a specific build flag, or that a service crashes without a particular env var, it saves that insight and uses it next time.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Alert-driven automation</h3><a id="user-content-alert-driven-automation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Alert-driven automation" href="#alert-driven-automation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When Alertmanager fires an alert labeled <code>kube-pilot: "true"</code>, kube-pilot receives a webhook and autonomously investigates. It queries Prometheus for metrics, searches Loki for error logs, checks pod state with kubectl, and attempts to fix the issue — all without human intervention. Add the label to any PrometheusRule to opt in.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Observability-aware debugging</h3><a id="user-content-observability-aware-debugging" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Observability-aware debugging" href="#observability-aware-debugging"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot has native access to your monitoring stack. When investigating any issue — whether from a GitHub issue or a firing alert — it can:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Query <strong>Prometheus</strong> via PromQL for CPU, memory, error rates, and custom metrics</li>
<li>Search <strong>Loki</strong> logs with <code>logcli</code> for errors, stack traces, and patterns</li>
<li>Check <strong>Alertmanager</strong> for active alerts and manage silences with <code>amtool</code></li>
<li>Create and update <strong>Grafana</strong> dashboards via the API</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Cloud infrastructure provisioning</h3><a id="user-content-cloud-infrastructure-provisioning" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Cloud infrastructure provisioning" href="#cloud-infrastructure-provisioning"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot can provision and manage real cloud infrastructure — not just deploy apps. With Crossplane enabled, it can create VPCs, databases, Kubernetes clusters, storage buckets, and any other cloud resource — all through kubectl, all through GitOps.</p>
<p dir="auto">Tested and validated: a single GitHub issue spun up a GKE Autopilot cluster on GCP in ~9 minutes. Credentials never touch a manifest — they flow through Vault → ExternalSecret → Crossplane ProviderConfig. The agent installs the right Crossplane Provider, wires up credentials, creates the resource, and polls until it's ready.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is the foundation for <strong>hub-and-spoke</strong> — a single k3s node running kube-pilot can provision and manage entire fleets of production clusters across AWS, GCP, and Azure.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Credential scrubbing</h3><a id="user-content-credential-scrubbing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Credential scrubbing" href="#credential-scrubbing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Before posting any comment or PR, kube-pilot scrubs known secrets and common credential patterns. Passwords, tokens, and API keys are redacted before they reach the LLM or any public output.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Automatic retry with backoff</h3><a id="user-content-automatic-retry-with-backoff" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Automatic retry with backoff" href="#automatic-retry-with-backoff"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Rate-limited by the LLM provider? kube-pilot retries with exponential backoff and respects <code>Retry-After</code> headers. No dropped tasks.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Failure recovery</h3><a id="user-content-failure-recovery" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Failure recovery" href="#failure-recovery"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If the agent crashes or hits an error, it posts a failure notice on the issue so nothing is silently orphaned.</p>

  --namespace kube-pilot --create-namespace \
  --set llm.apiKey=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --set gitea.gitea.admin.password=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>your-password<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot bootstraps itself: creates git repos, registers webhooks, provisions Grafana API keys, and starts listening. No manual setup.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Give it a task</h3><a id="user-content-give-it-a-task" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Give it a task" href="#give-it-a-task"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kubectl port-forward svc/kube-pilot-gitea-http -n kube-pilot 3000:3000"><pre>kubectl port-forward svc/kube-pilot-gitea-http -n kube-pilot 3000:3000</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>localhost:3000</code>, go to any repo, create an issue with the <code>kube-pilot</code> label:</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Title:</strong> Deploy a hello-world web server</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Body:</strong> Build a Go HTTP server that responds with <code>{"message":"hello"}</code> on port 8080. Deploy it to the default namespace.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Watch the issue. kube-pilot picks it up, does the work, and closes it when done.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Demo: CloudDesk office suite</h2><a id="user-content-demo-clouddesk-office-suite" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Demo: CloudDesk office suite" href="#demo-clouddesk-office-suite"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">We built <strong>CloudDesk</strong> — a multi-service office productivity suite — to demonstrate kube-pilot deploying and managing a real application across multiple repos. The source code and sample issues are in the <a href="/fbongiovanni29/kube-pilot/blob/main/demo"><code>demo/</code></a> directory.</p>

<p dir="auto">Expose deployed services externally with automatic DNS and TLS:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="traefik:
  enabled: true

certManager:
  enabled: true
  acmeEmail: you@example.com

externalDNS:
  enabled: true
  provider:
    name: cloudflare      # or aws, google, azure, digitalocean
  domainFilters:
    - apps.example.com
  # Credentials are loaded from the external-dns-credentials secret.
  # If using Vault, store them at kube-pilot/dns:
  #   vault kv put secret/kube-pilot/dns CF_API_TOKEN=xxx        (Cloudflare)
  #   vault kv put secret/kube-pilot/dns AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=xxx AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=xxx  (Route53)

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: traefik
  host: apps.example.com
  tls: true
  clusterIssuer: letsencrypt-prod"><pre><span class="pl-ent">traefik</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">enabled</span>: <span class="pl-c1">true</span>

<span class="pl-ent">certManager</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">enabled</span>: <span class="pl-c1">true</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">acmeEmail</span>: <span class="pl-s">you@example.com</span>

<span class="pl-ent">externalDNS</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">enabled</span>: <span class="pl-c1">true</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">provider</span>:
    <span class="pl-ent">name</span>: <span class="pl-s">cloudflare      </span><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> or aws, google, azure, digitalocean</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">domainFilters</span>:
    - <span class="pl-s">apps.example.com</span>
  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Credentials are loaded from the external-dns-credentials secret.</span>
  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> If using Vault, store them at kube-pilot/dns:</span>
  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span>   vault kv put secret/kube-pilot/dns CF_API_TOKEN=xxx        (Cloudflare)</span>
  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span>   vault kv put secret/kube-pilot/dns AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=xxx AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=xxx  (Route53)</span>

<span class="pl-ent">ingress</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">enabled</span>: <span class="pl-c1">true</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">className</span>: <span class="pl-s">traefik</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">host</span>: <span class="pl-s">apps.example.com</span>

  <span class="pl-ent">clusterIssuer</span>: <span class="pl-s">letsencrypt-prod</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">When ingress is enabled, kube-pilot automatically creates Ingress resources for deployed services with the pattern <code><service-name>.<domain></code>. cert-manager provisions TLS certificates via Let's Encrypt, and ExternalDNS creates DNS records — all automatically.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Observability</h3><a id="user-content-observability" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Observability" href="#observability"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">When observability is enabled:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The agent can query <strong>Prometheus</strong> (PromQL via curl) and create <strong>PrometheusRule</strong> CRs for new alert rules</li>
<li>The agent can search <strong>Loki</strong> logs using <code>logcli</code></li>
<li>The agent can manage <strong>Grafana</strong> dashboards via the API</li>
<li><strong>Alertmanager</strong> alerts labeled <code>kube-pilot: "true"</code> are routed to the agent's <code>/alertmanager-webhook</code> endpoint — firing alerts become autonomous investigation tasks</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Cloud infrastructure (Crossplane)</h3><a id="user-content-cloud-infrastructure-crossplane" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Cloud infrastructure (Crossplane)" href="#cloud-infrastructure-crossplane"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Provision cloud resources — VPCs, databases, Kubernetes clusters — directly from GitHub issues:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="crossplane:
  enabled: true"><pre><span class="pl-ent">crossplane</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">enabled</span>: <span class="pl-c1">true</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">That's it. Crossplane installs with sensible defaults. The agent handles the rest:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Installs the right Provider for your cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure)</li>
<li>Creates a ProviderConfig with credentials from Vault (never in manifests)</li>
<li>Provisions resources and monitors them until READY</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Store cloud credentials in Vault — the agent creates ExternalSecrets to sync them:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# GCP
vault kv put secret/crossplane/gcp creds=@gcp-sa-key.json

# AWS
vault kv put secret/crossplane/aws creds="$(printf '[default]\naws_access_key_id=%s\naws_secret_access_key=%s' $KEY $SECRET)""><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> GCP</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> AWS</span>
vault kv put secret/crossplane/aws creds=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">$(</span>printf <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>[default]\naws_access_key_id=%s\naws_secret_access_key=%s<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-smi">$KEY</span> <span class="pl-smi">$SECRET</span><span class="pl-pds">)</span></span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The agent knows how to work with Crossplane Providers, ProviderConfigs, Managed Resources, Composite Resources (XRDs), Compositions, and Claims. It understands READY/SYNCED status conditions, knows where to find provider logs, and follows the same GitOps workflow as everything else — manifests go through git, ArgoCD syncs them.</p>

    Prefer reading logs and metrics before making code changes.
    If the issue is ambiguous, ask a clarifying question instead of guessing.
    Keep tool calls minimal — don't explore when you can read.

    ... (your workflow, your rules, your tone)"><pre><span class="pl-ent">agent</span>:

<p dir="auto">Go template variables (<code>{{.GitProvider}}</code>, <code>{{.GiteaURL}}</code>, etc.) are available for git provider details. Dynamic sections (ingress URLs, observability endpoints, Crossplane guidance, repo context from <code>AGENTS.md</code>) are appended automatically — you don't need to include those.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Safety model</h2><a id="user-content-safety-model" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Safety model" href="#safety-model"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">kube-pilot is <strong>read-only against the cluster</strong> for persistent changes. All mutations go through git:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Every change is auditable (git history)</li>
<li>Every change is reversible (git revert)</li>
<li>ArgoCD is the only thing that writes to the cluster</li>
<li>Exception: Tekton TaskRuns (CI jobs), created directly by kube-pilot</li>
<li>Cloud infrastructure changes go through the same GitOps flow — Crossplane manifests are committed to git, ArgoCD syncs them, Crossplane reconciles</li>
<li>Cloud credentials never appear in manifests — they flow through Vault → ExternalSecret → ProviderConfig</li>
<li>Credentials are scrubbed before reaching the LLM and before any public output (comments, PRs)</li>
<li>Bot ignores its own webhook events (no self-triggering loops)</li>
</ul>
